Legacy puzzles and solutions — complete recovered catalogue

RETIRED CONTENT / FULL SPOILERS. Archived 24 October 2026. None of these puzzles, answers, rewards, room names, or progression rules are active in the new foundation.

This document covers two recovered local prototypes: A, the later three-room point-and-click opening; and B, the earlier 3D museum. Exact source commits and checksums are in source-manifest.json. The supplied shared-chat page could not be fetched; the recovered implementation and author atlas are the archival evidence. Completeness here means these recovered snapshots, not every unimplemented idea from every conversation.

Prototype A — the three-room opening

Source: source/three-room/core.mjs, art.mjs, and app.mjs. Original live project: https://puzzle-pieces-museum.johnmoore2048.chatgpt.site

Three exhibit rooms were open together after the tablet was collected. Five individual division paintings fed a sculpture; a hallway combined two murals; a food room combined four rebus paintings. Three physical map fragments completed the final cross-room clue.

A-xo / Xs and Os

  • Room: The Quotient Room; catalogue I; input type number.
  • Exact answer: 4.
  • Plaque: “Eight departures. Two returns.”

The horizontal line is a division bar. Count eight Xs above and two Os below: 8 ÷ 2 = 4. This establishes the visual grammar of the room.

A-flock / A Place to Return

  • Room: The Quotient Room; catalogue II; input type number.
  • Exact answer: 6.
  • Plaque: “No bird has ever owned a branch.”

Eighteen birds are above the branch that divides the painting. Three nests are beneath it. Count objects, not wings: 18 ÷ 3 = 6.

A-night / Borrowed Night

  • Room: The Quotient Room; catalogue III; input type number.
  • Exact answer: 3.
  • Plaque: “Even darkness has its share.”

Twelve stars sit above the horizon and four crescent moons below. The horizon is the division bar: 12 ÷ 4 = 3.

A-absence / A Study of Absence

  • Room: The Quotient Room; catalogue IV; input type number.
  • Exact answer: 7.
  • Plaque: “The little triangle belongs to the sky.”

The brass frame has turning studs. Rotate until the small gold triangle points up. Fourteen pale holes lie above the divider and two below: 14 ÷ 2 = 7. The empty spaces, rather than the dark material, are the objects being counted.

A-chromatic / Selective Memory

  • Room: The Quotient Room; catalogue V; input type number.
  • Exact answer: 2.
  • Plaque: “A blue hour. Everything warm is forgotten.”

Collect the blue inspection glass from the reception desk, then use it while viewing the painting. It isolates the blue marks from the rust-colored distractions. There are ten above the bar and five below: 10 ÷ 5 = 2. The colors are also distinguishable without the lens.

A-sculpture / The Weight of Answers

  • Room: The Quotient Room; catalogue VI; input type number.
  • Exact answer: 11.
  • Plaque: “Five works become one weight.”

The five blocks correspond to paintings I–V and display their accepted answers: 4, 6, 3, 7, 2. Add their weights (22) above the slab, and count two brass rings below. The same division rule gives 22 ÷ 2 = 11. The blocks are a visible feedback mechanism; entering 11 before the paintings are solved is allowed.

A-murals / Two Sides of the Same Thing

  • Room: The Long Division; catalogue VII; input type sequence.
  • Exact answer: 62533.
  • Plaque: “Like belongs to like. Begin where the light enters.”

The lit left mural gives the numerator order: leaves 18, birds 8, stars 20, drops 9, moons 12. The opposite mural scrambles their denominators: moons 4, leaves 3, drops 3, stars 4, birds 4. Match symbols, not positions, and divide in the left mural’s arrow direction: 18/3, 8/4, 20/4, 9/3, 12/4 → 62533. The single five-slot response is the only room answer.

A-banquet / The Unspoken Menu

  • Room: A Taste of Meaning; catalogue VIII; input type food.
  • Exact answer: 07080901.
  • Plaque: “Four courses. Their names have already been served.”

Read paintings I–IV as rebuses, then find each resulting food on the projection. I: an anvil squashes goo → squash, row 2 column 07. II: a sinking ship, an iceberg, and LET US → iceberg lettuce, row 4 column 08. III: black paint and a burial → black + bury → blackberry, row 1 column 09. IV: an egg-shaped factory → egg + plant → eggplant, row 3 column 01. Enter column numbers in painting order, not row order: 07 · 08 · 09 · 01.

A-way / The Way Through

  • Room: beyond; catalogue IX; input type word.
  • Exact answer: KEY.
  • Plaque: “No single room can show you the way out.”

Collect a map fragment from each completed room. When assembled, the three outlined glyphs ask for: the sculpture answer (11); the center of the five mural quotients (5); the sum of the four chosen food column numbers (7+8+9+1=25). The map’s alphabet strip converts 11,5,25 with A=1 → K,E,Y. Enter KEY. Every exhibit response and all three physical fragments are required before the next door opens.

Food room — exact individual works and projection

  • I / A Soft Landing (landing): “An unexpected impression.”
  • II / A Cold Reception (ship): “Sank from the same thing that got the Titanic.”
  • III / A Very Dark Funeral (burial): “The color of mourning. The act of mourning.”
  • IV / Industrial Life (factory): “Every morning, the plant produces another.”

Projection rows, columns 01–10 left to right:

  1. Pear · Plum · Lemon · Cherry · Banana · Orange · Fig · Grape · Blackberry · Apple
  2. Carrot · Potato · Onion · Beet · Broccoli · Peas · Squash · Corn · Radish · Pumpkin
  3. Eggplant · Egg · Pepper · Garlic · Mushroom · Tomato · Cucumber · Olive · Turnip · Chili
  4. Cabbage · Spinach · Kale · Arugula · Romaine · Chard · Watercress · Iceberg lettuce · Celery · Leek

The compound food answer is entered in artwork order, not projection row order. Squash → 07; iceberg lettuce → 08; blackberry → 09; eggplant → 01.

Murals — exact object groups

Left, in reading order: leaf × 18; bird × 8; star × 20; drop × 9; moon × 12.

Right, in physical order: moon × 4; leaf × 3; drop × 3; star × 4; bird × 4.

Gate, normalization, and recovery rules

All nine accepted responses plus all three physical room fragments are required to enter the final threshold. A correct answer does not automatically pick up its fragment. Sculpture answer 11 may be submitted before solving its paintings; the final gate still requires all responses. Numeric inputs allow harmless leading zeroes and trailing .0 forms. Sequence and word inputs ignore spaces and hyphens and use uppercase. Food accepts four columns 1–10, normalizing to two digits each. Source functions are retained for exact behavior.

The initial arrival includes an invitation, a tablet, a note, and a blue inspection glass. The long corridor’s far door deliberately loops. The further named wings are future chapters, not implemented puzzles. The fictional $100,000 invitation and earlier dedication/narrative are historical material, not adopted current story.

Puzzle Pieces — author atlas

Made for Tiffany. Complete spoilers; current playable collection.

Overall progression

Start in the Long Hall. Collect the plan and IV brochure from reception in the center of the hall. I, II and III can be solved in any order. Their three seals, the washroom card and the hanging-weight order converge in Security. Set ○ → ⌜ → ⋈ and submit to open the upper north terrace. Hold its south-facing, level view for 2.5 seconds. This marks the first visit; exploration continues.

The single south-wall public stair reaches only the west mezzanine. There are no bridges. East-side access requires Security acceptance and the employee stair. IV is public from the south-wall stair and supplies evidence for B1. Card → Security training and accepted print → South Service → inspection lift → manifest audit → clearance → freight to Upper. The same Security print releases the conference room, closet and garage: dispatch FRAME → workshop square CARE / AREA / REAR / EARN → secret Counterform return. Accepted inventory numbers restore only the local lower circuit. IV, the audit and circuit are not prerequisites for the terrace milestone.

The card opens Security only. The accepted sheet lights the service cable and releases the employee wing. The northern secret also waits for certification. Public lifts start isolated; restore their supply upstairs after using the employee stair. The conference-table key opens the glass gift shop. Staff stairs reach the loft, break room and optional third-floor rooms. South inspection always returns from B1.

Floor plans

Annotated four-floor SVG · Interactive author atlas

00 / Ground collection

Begin in the Long Hall. I, II and III can be solved in any order. The washroom credential opens Security in its separate approach corridor. Accepted redaction work releases the south service wing, garage and employee stair.

14 m central hall → intimate white galleries → 9.5 m light well / 11.5 m echo chamber. Secrets create two northern loops and two western returns. The 19 × 70 m hall has central reception, classical sculpture rows and a glass-fronted gift shop. The garage lies beyond the south service wing.

01 / Upper collection

The south-wall stair reaches IV. Security acceptance → South Service → employee stair reaches Lantern Walk, Projection Loft and employee rooms; the terrace waits for the three-seal security circuit.

Two separate upper ledges overlook the hall; no bridge connects them. Tall time galleries contrast with a 3.55 m staff kitchen. The freight landing is separate from the south inspection lift.

02 / Administration

Continue up the staff stair from the employee level. Both rooms are open once this circulation is reached; neither contains a mandatory lock or ending requirement.

An enclosed upper corridor deliberately leaves the public museum behind. The birthday room and administrator’s office provide context and corroboration.

B1 / The Uncatalogued

Complete Security training, have its final sheet accepted, then follow the lit floor cable through South Service and descend. Collect the manifest, audit all twelve objects and submit. Clearance opens freight; retained numbers restore the local circuit.

An unfinished 52 × 32 m receiving hall: worktables, exposed studs, packing debris and work lights. The inspection lift always returns to Ground.

Local exhibit progression

I / Chromatic Debt

Theme / mechanic: Complement · reversal · superposition.

  1. I1 / Pigment Room: Learn additive complements; make four reversed payments.
  2. I2 / Reverse Gallery: Verify reversal + complement; optionally reveal the blank-canvas switch.
  3. I3 / Light Well: Align the three masks; earn vermilion ⌜.
  4. I4 / Archive of Doubts: Optional archive loop returns through the North Arcade.

One of the three seals for Security. The archive is optional.

II / The Shape of Silence

Theme / mechanic: Delay · omission · return.

  1. II2 / Listening Gallery: Order the returning knocks to enter the deeper rooms.
  2. II3 / Echo Chamber: Identify pitch ranks, read missing voices, reverse the score.
  3. II4 / Resonance Vault: Record six notes; earn cobalt ○.
  4. II4 / Resonance Vault: Separately lend eight seconds of stillness; open the northern passage; its staff threshold still requires certification.

One seal plus an optional northern return after Security certification. Neither requires the other after the admission door.

III / Counterform

Theme / mechanic: Orientation · projection · witness.

  1. III1 / Counterform Gallery: Translate the north-down plan into a four-plate walk.
  2. III3 / Drafting Room: Check the stations; read three pinned frame orientations.
  3. III4 / The Absent Room: Rotate the fragments and hold the absent sitter’s viewpoint; earn chalk ⋈.
  4. III4 / The Absent Room: Open the inside latch for a direct return to the Long Hall.

One seal plus an independent shortcut. The Drafting Room can be read before solving the plates.

IV / In Perpetuity

Theme / mechanic: Elapsed time · recurrence · identity.

  1. IV1 / IV · In Perpetuity: Count the three elapsed sector delays and check their arithmetic.
  2. IV1 / IV · In Perpetuity: Set the dials; release the Afterimage Archive.
  3. IV2 / The Fifth Beat: Observe the five-beat signature and P/5 stamp, available from the start.
  4. IV3 / Afterimage Archive: Confirm the unauthorised transfer of the movement downstairs.

An optional archive and evidence for B1 item 06. No fourth seal or mandatory archive-visit flag.

V / The Uncatalogued

Theme / mechanic: Comparison · provenance · acceptance.

  1. V2 / Service Lift / B1: Complete Security training, then descend through South Service using the washroom card.
  2. V1 / V · The Uncatalogued: Collect the manifest; compare every arrival with its history and references.
  3. V1 / V · The Uncatalogued: Cross off fabrications and submit. Correct only the table groups that fail.
  4. V3 / Freight Lift / B1: Use issued clearance to open freight to the upper employee floor.
  5. V1 / V · The Uncatalogued: Enter retained numbers in ascending order to light the local circuit.

A new circulation loop and a local circuit state. Neither is required for the first-visit ending.

S / Security → Service Garage

Theme / mechanic: Redaction · letter deduction · word-square symmetry.

  1. S2 / Security: Make five computer lessons true, then print the sixth and submit it to the checker.
  2. G1 / Service Garage: Use the dispatch feedback and empty delivery to deduce FRAME.
  3. G2 / Letter Workshop: Arrange the sixteen tiles into matching four-word rows and columns.
  4. G3 / Counterform Service Passage: Return through the released passage into Counterform.

Security acceptance also enables South Service. The garage workshop is an optional branch. The employee stair, east mezzanine and public-lift supply are reached through the same service wing.

All locks and return routes

01 / The four-payment door (Puzzle)

  • Requires: Public access to the Pigment Room.
  • Action: Read Borrowed Primaries from right to left; press G → R → B → G on the physical reader.
  • Opens: Pigment Room → Reverse Gallery → Light Well.
  • Confirmation: White Lies demonstrates additive color mixing; return the missing primary, not the visible CMY field.
  • Recovery: An incorrect four-payment sequence clears after a short pause.

02 / The archive panels (Secret)

  • Requires: Reach the Reverse Gallery through lock 01. The color seal is not required.
  • Action: Swing Nothing to See away from the wall, then press the exposed button behind the canvas.
  • Opens: Opens the Archive of Doubts connections and the North Arcade loop.
  • Confirmation: The canvas edge and hinge are the mechanism. Receipt for a Missing Room confirms a second way out.
  • Recovery: The canvas can be opened and closed; the released passages stay open.

03 / Admission by echo (Puzzle)

  • Requires: Public East Approach → Listening Gallery.
  • Action: Strike the knockers separately; enter returns earliest first: II → IV → I → III.
  • Opens: Listening Gallery → Echo Chamber → Resonance Vault.
  • Confirmation: The second visual pulse returns after II 0.45 s, IV 0.80 s, I 1.20 s, III 1.65 s.
  • Recovery: An incorrect four-key admission clears after a short pause.

04 / The wall that listens (Secret)

  • Requires: Reach the Resonance Vault through lock 03. The sound seal is not required.
  • Action: Stand in the Lent Silence circle for 8 seconds without walking, looking or interacting.
  • Opens: Vault → North Cross Passage → North Service Passage. Its staff-stair door still requires Security acceptance; the secret cannot bypass certification.
  • Confirmation: Eight lamps count the uninterrupted seconds. Lantern Walk independently hints that silence hides a stair.
  • Recovery: Any movement, camera turn or interaction restarts the eight-second loan.

05 / The walk that opens a room (Puzzle)

  • Requires: Public access to Counterform. The Hinge Walk and Drafting Room are already open.
  • Action: Read the north-down plan, then walk the physical plates SW → NW → SE → NE. Leave a plate before entering the next.
  • Opens: Drafting Room → Absent Room.
  • Confirmation: Four Stations confirms point → line → triangle → ring, independently of map orientation.
  • Recovery: An incorrect four-plate walk clears after a short pause.

06 / The inside latch (Secret)

  • Requires: Enter the Absent Room through lock 05. The form seal is not required.
  • Action: Press the small brass latch on the hall-side wall from inside the Absent Room.
  • Opens: Absent Room → Long Hall; a permanent return shortcut.
  • Confirmation: The card describes a wall from its other side. No additional cipher or item is needed.
  • Recovery: Once released, the shortcut remains open.

07 / Security credential reader (Credential)

  • Requires: Pick up N. Ash’s level 02 card from the first washroom stall, beside the toilet.
  • Action: Use the card at the Security door in the small approach hallway south of the South Arcade.
  • Opens: Releases Security only. Staff circulation remains locked until the checker accepts the final redaction sheet.
  • Confirmation: The photograph is damaged but the magnetic strip remains intact. No serial-number entry is required.
  • Recovery: The credential remains usable. Neither the secret northern route nor the public elevator bank bypasses certification.

08 / The terrace collection circuit (Meta)

  • Requires: The physical card, all three original exhibit seals, and access to Security. Read the weights upstairs for their order.
  • Action: Set the three Security dials to ○ → ⌜ → ⋈; press the circular submit control.
  • Opens: Opens the north terrace door on the upper hall. The final viewpoint is a separate action on the terrace.
  • Confirmation: Weights for an Empty Room orders cobalt → vermilion → chalk from floor to ceiling; the earned marks provide the symbols.
  • Recovery: Wrong submissions leave the dials editable. IV and the basement are not prerequisites.

09 / South Service Door (Credential)

  • Requires: N. Ash’s card and an accepted final redaction sheet at the Security checker. No exhibit seals required.
  • Action: Submit the correct final sheet to the Security checker. Follow the illuminated copper floor cable to the released service door. Call the inspection car and use its interior button.
  • Opens: Security Approach → South Service → basement lift, employee stair, garage, supply closet and conference room. The hall-side employee door opens on the same circuit.
  • Confirmation: The Lower Service notice and wanted poster point to South Service. The basement route is now south, not at the old North Arcade proposal.
  • Recovery: The inspection lift always returns from B1; failed audits never close it.

10 / Three delays (Puzzle)

  • Requires: Public south-wall stair → upper west In Perpetuity. The Fifth Beat room is already open.
  • Action: Count vacant clockwise sectors from each red seam before the ivory hand; set the three physical dials to 3 / 1 / 4.
  • Opens: Fifth Beat room → Afterimage Archive.
  • Confirmation: Eight Rooms Ago: the total is 8; first minus second is 2; third minus first is 1.
  • Recovery: Dials cycle 0–5; matching all three opens the archive automatically. No seal is issued.

11 / Freight quarantine (Audit)

  • Requires: Collect the B1 manifest and submit a completely correct audit to the verifier.
  • Action: Cross off 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 09, 11. Retain 01, 07, 08, 10, 12. Feed the sheet into the physical verifier.
  • Opens: Issues curatorial clearance; opens B1 freight access and enables the freight lift between B1 and the upper employee hall.
  • Confirmation: All twelve object records and comparisons must agree. Red gauges identify incorrect table groups, not individual objects.
  • Recovery: Rejected sheets return after 2 seconds, with unlimited corrections. Marks freeze during verification and after acceptance.

12 / Night service authorisation (Puzzle)

  • Requires: Reach Security with the washroom card; complete its five computer lessons and print the sixth sheet.
  • Action: On the final sheet, redact the heavy statement’s “not”. Feed the printed sheet to the checker.
  • Opens: Releases the service wing and garage. The visible cable lights from the computer to the service door.
  • Confirmation: The hall has no bridge. Heavy “white is black” is literally false and therefore accepted after inversion.
  • Recovery: Rejected sheets return after two seconds with no penalty. Marked words can be restored.

13 / Dispatch plate (Puzzle)

  • Requires: Security authorisation opens the garage.
  • Action: Enter FRAME on the five-letter dispatch plate, using letter feedback and the empty delivery.
  • Opens: Garage → Letter Workshop.
  • Confirmation: The rack list contains the answer. Four timber sides and an absent canvas independently identify a frame.
  • Recovery: A full six-guess page can be cleared for unlimited further attempts.

14 / Crossed streets (Secret)

  • Requires: Enter the workshop through lock 13.
  • Action: Arrange all sixteen tiles as rows CARE / AREA / REAR / EARN and test the square.
  • Opens: Workshop → Counterform Service Passage → Hinge Walk. Both secret doors release.
  • Confirmation: Columns read the same words as rows; C and N fix opposite corners. Every word is in the brass register.
  • Recovery: Tiles can be exchanged or returned; failed checks keep the board intact.

15 / The shop inventory key (Credential)

  • Requires: Security acceptance gives access to the conference room.
  • Action: Collect the tagged brass key from the conference table, then return to the shop door in the South Arcade.
  • Opens: Opens the gift shop with its glass wall toward the Long Hall.
  • Confirmation: The closure card names the conference room; the meeting agenda mentions the misplaced key.
  • Recovery: The key remains collected and the shop stays open.

Room-by-room notes

H1 / The Long Hall

Arrival hub. Orientation / public and employee circulation.

Architecture: 19 × 70 m, 14 m high, limestone; floor 00.

Entry: Starting position faces north toward the tall window and original abstract statue.

  1. Read the left-hand welcome plaque, then walk to central reception for the plan and IV brochure.
  2. Explore I–III freely. The single stair on the south wall reaches only the west mezzanine and IV. Read its card at the west end.
  3. Observe classical sculpture studies, columns and newly hung abstract art. The glass gift shop is initially closed.
  4. The south-wall employee door remains locked until accepted work in Security. Return here after certification to visit the conference room.

Result: A 19 × 70 m, 14 m high hall with no bridge or east-side public stair. The east mezzanine requires the employee route.

Interpretation note: Additional canvases and classical studies enrich the collection; they do not introduce hidden code inputs. The plant story remains a future thread.

Clue cards: A note on the collection; The visitor plan; In Perpetuity / opening edition; Visitor, Absent; A stair with one destination; The gardener’s missing hour; Three suspensions; A statement held in suspension.

Lot 409 — every verdict and comparison

Reference A–F are image pairs; tables A–C group four arrivals each. Red gauges indicate only which group contains an error. Rejected sheets return after two seconds, can be revised freely and consume no resource.

01 / Gilded Nuremberg Chalice — RETAIN

Table A; reference A.

  • Record: Recorded in 1618 with six rubies. In 1631 the lower-right ruby was torn out; the broken claw was retained.
  • Observation: Five red stones. One empty setting with a torn claw.
  • Independent check: Damage entry 1631 / loss at lower right.

02 / Brass Mariner’s Astrolabe — CROSS OFF

Table A; reference A.

  • Record: Graduated 0, 30, 60, 90 clockwise. The painter accidentally reversed the final digits. No later alteration is recorded.
  • Observation: The brass scale reads 0, 30, 60, 06. Both digits are deeply engraved.
  • Independent check: Workshop calibration rubbing: 0 / 30 / 60 / 90.

03 / Delft Blue Porcelain Vase — CROSS OFF

Table A; reference B.

  • Record: The blue windmill was fired beneath the clear glaze. Its four sails were hand drawn; no stencil was used.
  • Observation: A lifted edge of blue paint sits above the clear glaze. A small overspray crescent touches the foot.
  • Independent check: Stencil packet in the waste bin: LOT 409 / 03. Its torn sail and overspray crescent match.

04 / Ceremonial Boar Dagger — CROSS OFF

Table A; reference B.

  • Record: The Huntsman panel was copied directly from a mirror. FRONT is engraved at the guard: all sides in the audit are viewed from this marked face.
  • Observation: FRONT faces you. The boar is on the left side of the pommel, as it is in the painted mirror image.
  • Independent check: Original smith’s rubbing, viewed from FRONT: boar on right.

05 / Bust of Seneca — CROSS OFF

Table B; reference C.

  • Record: The delivered object was a single carved stone. No moulding, hollow shell or material replacement is authorised.
  • Observation: A vertical mould seam runs behind the ear. A chip curls like wax beside a WAX / 409-05 casting sleeve.
  • Independent check: The lamp illuminates a wax test casting beside a signed stone offcut. Read the seam as well as the light.

06 / Chiming Pocket Watch — CROSS OFF

Table B; reference C.

  • Record: The sealed original mechanism repeats four equal ticks; there is no fifth accent. The movement has never been replaced.
  • Observation: Four short beats followed by a deeper fifth. A service window shows P/5 — 2024 on the movement.
  • Independent check: Compare The Fifth Beat upstairs. The exhibition brochure identifies that mechanism and its five-pulse signature.

07 / Velvet & Ermine Crown — RETAIN

Table B; reference D.

  • Record: The painted cross was straight. Transit report: crate 07 was closed below the cross; compression bent it toward the split hinge.
  • Observation: The cross bends left. Fresh gold transfer remains under crate 07’s low lid at the same angle.
  • Independent check: Crate 07 / transit photograph and matching scrape beneath the lid.

08 / Ivory Chess Queen — RETAIN

Table B; reference D.

  • Record: This particular tapestry was woven from the back of its cartoon. The displayed reference is the reversed face; compare the same front of the figure.
  • Observation: The queen’s sceptre is on the left. The woven reference puts it on the right.
  • Independent check: Loom slip: REVERSED FACE. The original cartoon has its sceptre on the left.

09 / Verdigris Bronze Mirror — CROSS OFF

Table C; reference E.

  • Record: Solid bronze with a chased relief. Museum accession tags are tied on; nothing is cast into the base.
  • Observation: Under the base: CAST 2024 / RESIN REPLICA / 409-09. The letters are moulded into the object, beneath a barcode.
  • Independent check: A tilted inspection mirror on the bench reveals the underside; the close-up also includes this view.

10 / Ebony & Pearl Lute — RETAIN

Table C; reference E.

  • Record: Restrung in 1890 as ten paired courses plus one single chanterelle: twenty-one strings and twenty-one pegs. The painter showed only nine.
  • Observation: Two rows of ten pegs, with a single peg at the tip. Twenty-one strings meet the bridge.
  • Independent check: 1890 restorer’s tally: 10 × 2 + 1 = 21. All twenty-one peg holes show use.

11 / Alchemist’s Retort Flask — CROSS OFF

Table C; reference F.

  • Record: Hollow Venetian glass. Certified empty mass 310 g. The packing scale was checked at zero with the identical empty tray.
  • Observation: The scale reads 1,420 g. The transparent vessel contains a solid core, extending into the neck.
  • Independent check: A 310 g reference weight reads 310 g on the adjacent test scale. No liquid or loose packing remains inside.

12 / Silver Guild Seal Matrix — RETAIN

Table C; reference F.

  • Record: The red impression shows a lion facing left. The die is read straight on from its engraved stamping face.
  • Observation: The recessed lion faces right. A fresh impression beside it faces left.
  • Independent check: The casting and its impression meet as mirror partners; the old impression agrees.

Retain 01, 07, 08, 10, 12. The five contacts accept 1 → 7 → 8 → 10 → 12. Clearance enables the separate freight lift; the circuit illuminates locally without opening a further room.

I / Chromatic Debt

Studies in borrowed light · Ground collection · perception / subtraction

A color is not what it owns, but what it withholds. Three witnesses leave four debts. Begin at the end; pay only the missing voice.

On the other side, the world keeps what this side has spent. The back reverses the order and the testimony. Each witness may turn; each may recant.

When the accounts agree, the upper edge confirms the whole. An unpainted surface may still have an edge. A number withdrawn from the collection cannot grant admission.

II / The Shape of Silence

Studies for an absent audience · Ground collection · omission / return

The visitor makes one arrival; the room makes another. Admit the returns from earliest to latest, never by the haste of the hand.

Beyond the threshold, ink records the voices refused. Height belongs to sound, not to the body making it. What returns must retrace its journey.

Six vacancies make a performance. Their intervals keep a second account. In the last circle, eight seconds must pass without a contribution. Silence is also a kind of key.

A statement survives its ink

Security / training circular · Read before the night audit

Every surviving statement must be true. An empty sheet says nothing and proves nothing.

Touch a word to cover it. Its punctuation belongs to it. Touch the bar to restore it. Line breaks are only spacing; a surviving period ends a statement. Without it, the next line continues the thought.

The allowance counts covered words, not gestures. Each sheet prints its own limit.

Weight is not emphasis

Department of Verification · Heavy-ink register · introduced on sheet III

The first two calibration screens use one ordinary display weight. From sheet III, the contrast matters.

Read a heavy statement literally, then reverse its truth value. Heavy type is a denial of the whole statement. Covering a word does not lift that denial.

Ordinary: white is white.
Heavy: white is black.
Both can be admitted.

Prototype B supplement — exact six redaction sheets

Punctuation belongs to its word. Surviving periods end statements; removing a terminal word can join two lines. From lesson III, heavy statements invert their literal truth value. Mixed-weight or unrecognized statements fail. The sheet cannot be empty.

Limit: 1 word. Complete on the computer.

  • true.
  • false.

Delete: token 1, “false.”.

Surviving statement(s): “true”.

B-redaction-2 / Calibration / II

Limit: 3 words. Complete on the computer.

  • white is not white.
  • black is white.

Delete: token 3, “white.”; token 5, “is”; token 6, “white.”.

Surviving statement(s): “white is not black”.

B-redaction-3 / Heavy ink / III

Limit: 1 word. Complete on the computer.

  • true.
  • HEAVY: black is not white.

Delete: token 3, “not”.

Surviving statement(s): “true”; “black is white” (heavy, so invert literal truth).

B-redaction-4 / A statement about this room / IV

  • the hall has no windows.

Delete: token 3, “no”.

Surviving statement(s): “the hall has windows”.

B-redaction-5 / A statement about a work / V

  • below vermilion.

Reuse procedure

Refer to a stable legacy ID or exact atlas title, copy the idea into a new proposed puzzle design record, and explicitly approve its new location, rules, answer destination, and progression role. Do not import old save data or silently make old keys, seals, or codes necessary.
